upstream.entrypoint: evaluate(prediction: str, scoring_points: str) -> (passing, failing, score)

method: Fetch the file at the pinned commit: GET https://api.github.com/repos/microsoft/OpenRCA/contents/main/evaluate.py?ref=c121a483a5a91dbae50708e5942c42a6609098b2 (base64 content).
importlib-load it as a module; it needs only `re` and `itertools` for `evaluate()`.
Call `evaluate(case.prediction, case.scoringPoints)` for every case below.
Record `passing`, `failing` and `score` verbatim; `score` is upstream's own round(x, 2).
packages/core/test/openrca-evaluator.test.ts replays this file through this repository's scorer and requires every score to be reproduced.

differences.why: The evaluator recovers the block with a non-greedy regex, so a reason containing a double quote is truncated and its criterion is lost. This repository parses the cell as JSON, which recovers the reason the exporter wrote. Reproducing the truncation would score a correct answer lower for being correct, so the difference is declared rather than copied.

The evaluator's regex finds a JSON block anywhere in the cell; this repository requires the cell to parse as JSON. The exporter writes a JSON document, so an export is unaffected -- but a hand-written or model-written answer that wraps its block in prose scores lower here than upstream. Closing it means re-implementing the regex, which is the reader the first difference argues against; the direction is stated so a decision to change it is visible.
